cut_items.item: Save the key before the first call so retries (including from queues/job runners) read the same stored key
Stripe stores and replays the first result including errors: after a card decline, same key returns same decline, so use a new key only for a new customer attempt
Use an order-based key rather than per-click key so double clicks/repeated browser requests don't create two charges
SDKs can retry automatically and reuse the key; configure maxNetworkRetries in Node/Python/Ruby libraries
Stripe recommends PaymentIntents over legacy Charges API, which supports the same idempotency keys
Explains why: network error/timeout doesn't reveal whether Stripe received or charged the request
Key can be a UUID or derived from order ID; creating new key inside retry loop is the most common mistake
Stripe stores and replays the first result, including errors. A retry with the same key after a card decline returns the same decline, so a new key is needed when the customer starts a new attempt
Save the key before the first call and make sure queue or job-runner retries read the saved key
Do not generate a new key inside the retry loop, which Y calls the most common mistake
Use an order-based key rather than a per-click key, so double clicks or repeated browser requests do not create two charges
Set maxNetworkRetries in the official SDKs (Node, Python, Ruby), which retry and reuse the key
Stripe recommends PaymentIntents over the older Charges API, and PaymentIntents support idempotency keys
A network error or timeout does not tell you whether Stripe received the first request
Suggests a UUID as the key

added_items.item: Retries after 5xx errors or timeouts are safe with the same key
Retries after a 5xx error or timeout are safe with the same key
Suggests a key derived from the order or cart ID (also in Y as order ID)
